A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DetailMaster and provide readable text, tables, figures, and complete appendices. Content can be reliably matched despite substantial reformatting and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of twelve generators, human assessment of benchmark quality, and pipeline ablation and robustness experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds generator evaluations, controlled training experiments, short-prompt testing, and evaluator analyses.

M1.justification: v3 introduces an ablation-specific SD-XL adaptation combining T5 and CLIP through a Timestep-Aware Semantic Connector, training only the connector while freezing the backbone and encoders (Appendix C.2). The benchmark construction and main evaluation algorithms remain unchanged; expanded filtering descriptions document the existing pipeline.

E1.justification: v3 newly evaluates short-prompt generalization on T2I-CompBench, covering attribute binding, spatial and non-spatial relationships, and complex composition (Appendix U). The original source datasets, 4,116-prompt benchmark, four evaluation dimensions, and 800-prompt mini-benchmark are retained.

E2.justification: The twelve original generators remain. Table 2 adds SANA, Qwen-Image, Janus-1.3B, JanusFlow-1.3B, Janus-Pro-1B, Lumina-Image-2.0, and BAGEL-7B-MoT; Appendix Q additionally evaluates Nano Banana 2. Qwen-Image also enters the cross-evaluator comparison, substantially expanding the evaluated methods.

E3.justification: v3 adds a controlled 2×2 design varying 77/512-token limits and short/long training captions, with two million sampled training pairs and short captions compressed to at most 30 tokens (Appendix C.2). Additional protocols include T2I-CompBench evaluation and a 3B evaluator. Nano Banana 2 uses model-chosen resolution rather than the fixed resolution specified for earlier comparisons.

E4.justification: New analyses test training versus context capacity, short-prompt generalization, missing attributes in source captions, Qwen-Image evaluator-family bias, and smaller-evaluator robustness. Figures 7–8 extend length-sensitivity analysis to seven additional generators. Existing detector/cropping ablations, difficulty analysis, and illustrated case studies are retained.

E5.justification: The same three listed evaluator runs for five generators at temperature 0.8 remain in v2 Table 10 and v3 Table 13. No new uncertainty intervals, significance tests, or seed-reporting practices appear. The additional smaller-evaluator Kendall correlations reuse an existing reporting approach.

E6.justification: The original twelve-model Table 2 scores and matched appendix tables are unchanged. v3 adds substantial results, including Qwen-Image's 60.04% relationship accuracy, controlled ablation outcomes, T2I-CompBench scores, missing-attribute rates, evaluator comparisons, and additional length curves. Nano Banana 2's Table 18 scores are new results under its variable-resolution setting.

T1.justification: Appendix B retains the same region coordinates, 75% coverage criterion, and spatial-assignment reasoning. No substantive mathematical revisions or proofs are added. The prompt/constraint notation introduced in Appendix G restates the existing prompt-conditioned evaluation objective.

C1.justification: v3 drops the claim to be the first such benchmark and narrows the abstract's encoder-failure statement to weak encoders. It explicitly emphasizes synergy between expanded context and long-prompt training. The central benchmark contribution and claims about compositional failures and declining adherence with prompt length remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations of advanced encoders, unified architectures, and Nano Banana 2's positional and attribute-binding failures (Appendices O–Q). It develops arguments about evaluator-family bias and smaller-evaluator viability, and explicitly bounds the benchmark as a proxy for professional constraint-intensive prompts. Sections 4.4–4.5 also make more assertive mechanistic and training interpretations.

D1.justification: Appendix C.2 documents the new connector, frozen components, training-data construction, and caption compression. Appendices E and V add verification prompts and worked filtering examples. The embedded code link changes from Data-Juicer's DetailMaster branch to Qirui-jiao/DetailMaster. Existing hardware, timing, and core inference disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds ConceptMix, LongBench-T2I, T2I-CoReBench, and OneIG-Bench, expanding positioning beyond v2's DensePrompts/DPG-Bench discussion. It develops new distinctions concerning synthetic prompt sources, physical plausibility, constraint density, and evaluation granularity. References supporting newer generator architectures and proposed research directions also expand.

P1.justification: v3 substantially rewrites the abstract and introduction, revises related-work and conclusion passages, and reorganizes contributions and model categories. Existing conditional-attribute analysis and evaluator-bias discussion move into appendices. The appendix organization changes extensively, and the standalone contents page and Limitations heading disappear, with several underlying caveats retained elsewhere.

P2.justification: The main text switches to a two-column conference layout. Table 2 is reorganized into five model groups; new tables and Figures 7–8 appear; Figure 6 receives standardized vertical axes; and old Table 3 becomes appendix Table 20. Existing case-study images are rearranged from 4×3 to 6×2 grids.

improvement.justification: v2's training-versus-context argument relied on comparisons between heterogeneous generators. v3 adds a controlled SD-XL ablation and short-prompt transfer testing, substantially strengthening this central argument, alongside broader generator and evaluator validation. Some interpretation remains overstated: Table 3's 77-token long-trained configuration trails the 512-token short-trained configuration on background and style despite the claim of consistent superiority. This qualification limits the conclusion but does not outweigh the substantial improvement in empirical support and documentation.
